entries.gave: Read the Cut, the five decisions and the package invoicer (lines.parse_lines, tax.tax_of with a fraction rate, totals, render, pyproject with no scripts entry, no tests). Its people: accounting colleagues who save the lines from a spreadsheet and run one command with the client tax rate to print the invoice, and the developer who installs it once per machine with pipx.
Read code/best-practice.md with template.md (N1-N8) and refactor-code/best-practice.md (N1-N8) to their end before any change.
pyproject.toml gives no test command, nor does README.md (it says only Playground), and the cut names no architecture.
find finds no test_*.py and no Test strategy exists, so the runner is the one that comes with Python: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . (stdlib, Python 3.14 on the machine).
Ran the runner by throwaway.py: no tests exist yet, so none ran; no failing test, nothing to ask.

No architecture or unit cases exist, so from the request and the cut I wrote the unit cases of the command first: prints the invoice of the lines at the rate given; reads a rate with a percent sign; takes rate 0 and 100 (ends); refuses a rate above 100, below 0, not a number, NaN; refuses a run without a rate; refuses a missing file, a file not saved as UTF-8, a file with no lines; reads a file with a byte order mark; prints nothing when a row is wrong. And of lines.parse_lines: reads rows, skips blank rows, refuses a row of other than three fields, a price that is no number written with a point, a quantity that is no whole number from 1, each naming the row. The trace: the cut and invoicer/ read to their end.

Decisions left to the code: how the rate is written on the command line (a percent, 0 to 100, as accounting says it, with or without %, over the fraction tax_of takes); how the command takes the file and rate (invoicer LINES --rate PERCENT); the text encoding read (UTF-8, a byte order mark allowed, as spreadsheets save CSV UTF-8); which values a row refuses (price a finite number with a point, quantity a whole number from 1); the form and exit code of a refusal (argparse error: usage, then invoicer: error: <file>, row N: ..., exit 2).

One new module, invoicer/command.py, decides what the command takes from whoever runs it and what it prints, as it can change while the parse, tax and render stay. The row format and what a row refuses stay in invoicer/lines.py, which already decides it. Tax, totals and render stay as they are.
No decision has variants that the cases call for now (one input form, one output), so no pattern and no variant modules.

Offered: invoicer.command.main (the pyproject script entry and the tests call it), invoicer.lines.parse_lines, Line and the new LineError (command.py and tests call them). Internal: command._parser, command._percent, command._read, lines._price, lines._quantity.

Planned: the LINES argument and --rate (cases: prints the invoice, refuses a run without a rate); the % suffix (case: reads a rate with a percent sign); the 0-100 check (cases at both ends and beyond); the NaN/infinite check (case: refuses NaN); the UTF-8 with BOM read (cases: BOM, not UTF-8); the missing-file catch (case); the no-lines refusal (case). Dropped: a --currency option, an output file, a comma decimal reading, a header row skip: no case asks for them.

No module is added inside the part beyond command.py, whose cases are the unit cases; lines.parse_lines cases support test_prints_nothing_when_a_row_is_wrong: test_reads_each_row_as_a_line, test_skips_a_blank_row, test_refuses_a_row_of_two_fields_naming_it, test_refuses_a_price_written_with_a_comma_naming_the_row, test_refuses_a_price_that_is_not_finite, test_refuses_a_quantity_that_is_not_whole, test_refuses_a_quantity_of_zero (the end of the class from 1).
No case is needed that supports no unit case; nothing to ask.
Inputs from outside: the LINES path and --rate text, both in command.main via argparse; the file content, read in command._read; each row of it, in lines.parse_lines.

Things and names: an invoice line (Line, line, lines); a row of the saved file (row, in parse_lines); the tax rate as a fraction (rate in tax_of, total, render); the tax rate as accounting types it (would also be rate).
The cut says line and row as the code does (one row per line), and the tax rate; README.md holds only Playground.
No thing has two names: line and row stay apart as the cut keeps them (row of the file, line of the invoice).

rate would name two things, the fraction and the percent typed: rate keeps the fraction, as tax_of and render use it; the typed one is percent in command.py, and the option is --rate as the cut says the tax rate.

Rules and where written: the row format <description>;<price>;<quantity> (lines.py docstring and split), the cent rounding (tax.py CENT), the column layout (render.py), the percent-to-fraction (command.py only).
The places alike: subtotal plus tax_of in totals.total and in render.render, both change with the tax rule, as each calls tax_of; the 30/12 widths in render.py repeat on each row and change together.

The row format and its refusals stay in lines.py, whose job it is; the refusal message names the field separator from one constant there. The percent reading stays in command.py, the one module that takes typed input. render.py and totals.py are outside this cut and keep their own layout; left as they are.
Kinds done in many places: reporting a wrong input, checking an input, laying out a module (docstring sentence first), laying out a test.
Ways now: reporting a wrong input, parse_lines lets ValueError or decimal.InvalidOperation escape with no row; no other check exists. Modules all open with a one-line docstring; no tests exist.
No style settings for Python (lefthook only skips japanese), so the code ways stay: a one-line module docstring first, plain functions, Decimal for money.

A new way for a wrong input: lines.LineError (a ValueError) naming the row, raised for every row refusal, which the command turns into one argparse error, so every refusal of the command reads invoicer: error: ... and exits 2; it removes the fault that the escaping errors named no row. Tests: unittest, one TestCase per module.

Took the five decisions of the cut as they stand and settled the rest from the purpose: the command invoicer LINES --rate PERCENT installed by a pyproject script entry for pipx; the rate typed as a percent 0-100, with or without %; the file read as UTF-8 with a byte order mark allowed; each wrong row refused with its row number before printing; refusals as argparse errors, exit 2. Nothing left open, so no asks.

Module openings: command.py "What the invoicer command takes from whoever runs it, and what it prints."; lines.py "The lines of an invoice, and which rows of text, <description>;<price>;<quantity>, give one." Each names one decision.

Changes tried on first sentences alone: a new option such as --currency names command.py; a fourth column or comma decimals names lines.py; another rounding names tax.py; another layout names render.py. Each names one module.

Types on each offered name: main(argv: Sequence[str] | None) -> None; parse_lines(text: str) -> list[Line]; Line(description: str, price: Decimal, quantity: int = 1), amount() -> Decimal; ROW: str; LineError(ValueError).

Docstrings of main and parse_lines say Takes, Gives (the empty case: [] where every row is blank), and Refuses (SystemExit 2 with usage and invoicer: error: ..., nothing on stdout; LineError naming the row from 1, blank rows counted).

Checked each test against the docs: row numbers counting blank rows, the order of lines, the [] for blank text, the % suffix, the 0 and 100 ends, exit 2 with nothing on stdout are each stated in the docstrings; nothing relied on only the body.
Wrote LineError alone first and saw the lines tests fail, then the body of lines.py; a stub main(argv) that did nothing and saw 14 command tests fail, then the body of command.py.
Ran python3 -m unittest discover -s tests by throwaway.py after each body: 9 lines tests OK, then all 23 OK, and again after each refactor step. The trace: tests run.
Read each body: every branch answers a case (the % suffix, NaN, the 0-100 ends, the missing file, not UTF-8, no lines, each row refusal); no option or fallback without a case, none removed.

pyproject.toml: [project.scripts] invoicer = invoicer.command:main, [tool.setuptools] packages = [invoicer], and a head comment: Python 3.9 or later, no other package, pipx install, and the test command. No lock file, as the code has no dependency.
Each command test makes its own temporary folder in setUp and removes it by addCleanup; the lines tests touch no file.
The tests run no real tool beyond Python itself; nothing to turn off.
Ran the 23 tests three times in shuffled orders, seeds 11, 2026 and 90817 printed: 0 failed each time.

In a throwaway copy with an empty home: pip install --target of the repository by its setup alone (the machine has no venv or pipx) gave bin/invoicer, which printed the invoice; the tests passed there. Nothing missing from the setup.
One test per case: 9 in tests/test_lines.py, 14 in tests/test_command.py, each name saying its case with no and.

Expected values worked from the cases by hand before running: 100.00x2 + 10.50 = 210.50; at 19% 39.995 rounds half up to 40.00, total 250.50; at 7.7% 16.2085 gives 16.21; at 100% 210.50 and 421.00; at 0% 0.00.
Each test keeps its rate, rows and expected text in its body; shared helpers only build the temporary file (saved), run main capturing output (run_command), and lay out a printed row (row).
No loop or branch in any test body; each input is a test of its own (rate above 100, negative, not a number, NaN).
Failure messages where the values alone do not say it: the refused rate is named; 210.50 at 7.7% is 16.2085.

Ran the tests before the code: lines refusals failed by LineError not raised, ValueError of unpacking and of int(2.5); command tests failed by exit 0 where 2 was due and empty output; the three reading tests passed, pinning what parse_lines already did. The trace: tests run.
Tests use the real modules and real files in their own temporary folder; no test double, as nothing is slow or outside.
Tests reach only main, parse_lines, LineError and the fields of Line that callers read; no internal name (_rate, _price, _line) is called.
Changed a body without its interface: extracted lines._line out of parse_lines and moved the row form into ROW; all 23 tests still passed, none rewritten.
Each test asserts the whole result of its Then: the full printed invoice text, the full list of lines, the exact refusal message with exit 2 and empty stdout.

No Test strategy names a tool; ran coverage.py (installed only in the throwaway home) with --branch: command.py 100%, lines.py 98% (line 25 Line.__repr__), totals.py 71% (lines 15-16 total), render.py and tax.py 100%. The trace: coverage run.

The lines no test runs, Line.__repr__ and totals.total, are older names the package offers in __all__ for callers outside this cut; no case of the cut calls them, and removing them could break those callers, so they stay untouched. Every new line and branch is run.
No Test strategy exists, so none names an interface for property-based tests; none written.
No property-based test ran, so no failing input to weigh.
The round takes no CI report of mutation testing (CI runs only lint), so there are no surviving mutants to list.
No mutant listed by N7.6, nothing to name or remove.
No mutant listed by N7.6, nothing to mark as changing nothing.
No mutant listed by N7.6, no test to tighten.

Each input is read into its inside form where it comes in: --rate into a Decimal fraction by argparse type=_rate; the file into text by open(utf-8-sig); each row into a Line of str, finite Decimal and int from 1 by lines._line, _price, _quantity; no raw text reaches render.
Refused, not guessed: a price with a comma (10,50 could be ten and a half or a thousands mark), a rate with a comma, NaN or infinity, a quantity of 1.5 or +3 or 0, a row of other than three fields.
main catches only FileNotFoundError, UnicodeDecodeError and LineError, each by its type, as each tells accounting what to fix; any other error stops with its trace. No bare except.
Each message says the program, what, where and what is accepted, such as: invoicer: error: lines.csv, row 3: the price must be a number written with a point, such as 12.50, not ten.
Every check is an if that raises (LineError, ArgumentTypeError, parser.error); no assert.

Ran the installed invoicer command with a comma price, a header row, two fields, quantity 1.5, an empty file, a Latin-1 file, a missing file, no --rate, rate 0.19x and 120: each exits 2 with nothing printed, and each message alone says the row or argument and what to write instead.

Before the structure steps (extract _line, ROW constant, LineError in __init__): grep of parse_lines and Line found no test before this work; the reading of rows, blank-row skipping and stripping had none.

Pinned what parse_lines did before any change: test_reads_each_row_as_a_line (spaces stripped, Decimal price, int quantity), test_skips_a_blank_row, test_gives_no_line_for_a_text_of_blank_rows; they passed against the old body.
Structure steps taken one at a time, each leaving the tests runnable: extract lines._line; add ROW and use it in lines and command; export LineError from __init__.
No step renamed a name a test uses; no expected result changed.
Ran the tests after the steps: 23 OK; none failed, nothing undone.

No behavior looked wrong against its name, the cut or its callers; the row refusals that now raise LineError (a ValueError) in place of a bare ValueError or decimal.InvalidOperation are the change that decision N8 asks for, not a structure step, and are put in the Made for sign-off.

grep of each name: every new name is used (_SEPARATOR, ROW, _WHOLE, _line, _price, _quantity, _parser, _rate, LineError); Line.__repr__ and totals.total are offered by __all__ to outside callers, so kept.
No function only passes its call on: _parser builds the options, _line splits and checks a row, _price and _quantity check one field each.
No parameter is given the same value at every call; the number parameter of _price and _quantity varies by row, and argv of main is None from the entry point and a list from tests.
Comments kept say what code cannot: why utf-8-sig, why ASCII digits only, what ROW is shown for, how the test sum rounds; none repeats its code.
Read each name where used: percent (the rate as typed), rate (the fraction), row (a text row), number (its row number), saved (the open file), wrong (the LineError), run_command, saved, row in tests.
Each matched its definition; the loop result was named found and became a comprehension with _line, and args became arguments; no other rename needed.
One rename only: the typed tax rate is percent in command._rate, the fraction keeps rate as in tax_of and render; messages say the tax rate.

One sentence each: main reads the arguments and file into lines and prints their invoice or refuses; _parser builds the command line; _rate turns a typed percent into a fraction; parse_lines gives the line of each non-blank row; _line, _price, _quantity check one row or field; each test checks one case.
No line stopped the reading; the comprehension in parse_lines has one filter and one call, and the 0 <= value <= 100 check reads plainly.
parse_lines read rows and checked each field in one: extracted _line, _price and _quantity, each named for its task. main reads, refuses and prints, steps a caller never wants apart, so it stays one.
No function reads a global setting; the row number each check names is passed in as number.
parse_lines mixed the loop over rows with the field checks; the checks moved into _line, _price and _quantity, so each line of parse_lines and main is one step.
Each one-caller function (_parser, _rate, _line, _price, _quantity) has a name that says what it gives without its caller; none folded back.
Marked as odd to a stranger: encoding utf-8-sig in place of utf-8; the [0-9]+ regex where int() would do; value = None after InvalidOperation.
The digits regex is a named constant, _WHOLE; value = None lets one message serve both a non-number and a non-finite number, plain from the if below it.
Comments where no name says the reason: utf-8-sig drops the byte order mark that a spreadsheet CSV UTF-8 starts with; _WHOLE is ASCII only, as int() also takes digits of other scripts.
Every marked line had its reason, so none is left for an asks.
Read each docstring against its code: the parse_lines docstring now says spaces dropped around each field, the refusals, and the row numbering, as the body does; none stale.
The row form is written once as lines.ROW, from _SEPARATOR, and command.py imports it for its no-line message and help; the separator is written once as _SEPARATOR.
No shared function takes a flag that picks a branch.
No module uses another module internal name; command.py uses only ROW, LineError, parse_lines and render, all offered.
Every place that needs a rule is Python and reads one definition; the pyproject entry names invoicer.command:main, which main docstring says.

Each refusal is written the chosen way: rows raise LineError naming the row, the command turns every refusal into parser.error (or ArgumentTypeError for --rate), so each reads invoicer: error: ... with exit 2; tests are unittest TestCases.
One place keeps a different way, with its reason in its docstring: _rate raises argparse.ArgumentTypeError, not parser.error, so that argparse names the option --rate in the message.

Made invoicer/command.py (invoicer LINES --rate PERCENT), row refusals with row numbers in invoicer/lines.py (LineError, ROW), LineError exported in invoicer/__init__.py, the pipx-installable entry point in pyproject.toml, and 23 tests in tests/test_lines.py and tests/test_command.py, all passing.

Tried by throwaway.py as accounting would: the command installed from the setup alone, a file as a spreadsheet saves CSV UTF-8 (byte order mark, CRLF), invoicer acme-november.csv --rate 19 and --rate 7.7%: exit 0, totals 2390.47 and 2163.48, checked by hand; each wrong input exits 2 with a message naming what to fix; 23 tests OK. Nothing to mend.

Wrote the Made in rounds/invoicer/1/made.json: where each of the five decisions lands, no More kept, and eight points settled with their grounds (rate as percent, command line, price with a point, quantity from 1, UTF-8 with BOM, LineError, refusal form, tests).
